title: Transformer Architecture
interviewAnswer: Transformers combine attention, feed-forward networks, residual connections and normalization. Encoder-only, decoder-only and encoder-decoder variants serve different tasks.
why: Transformers are central to modern NLP, vision and generative AI; you should be able to explain the block, not only self-attention.
intuition: Each token first gathers context through attention, then independently passes through a feed-forward network. Residual connections and normalization stabilize deep stacks.
deepDive: A transformer block typically contains multi-head attention, position-wise feed-forward layers, residual connections and normalization. Attention projects hidden states to Q/K/V, computes compatibility and mixes values. Multiple heads learn different subspaces. Encoders use bidirectional attention; autoregressive decoders apply causal masks. Positional information is required because plain attention has no inherent sequence order.
workedExample: In a causal language model, token t can attend to positions ≤t but not future tokens; the causal mask enforces next-token prediction semantics.
commonMistakes: Explaining a transformer as “just attention” and omitting FFN/residual/norm.
Forgetting causal masking in decoder-only language models.
Saying attention gives order without positional information.
production: Transformer inference cost grows with sequence length; batching, KV cache, quantization and context management are major serving concerns.
